snippets.output: Clear urine can be a sign of several conditions or behaviors, including high fluid intake, diabetes insipidus, diuretic use, alcohol consumption, and certain medical conditions.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of causes/conditions for clear urine.

snippets.output: High fluid intake is one of the most common reasons for clear urine. When you drink a lot of water, your kidneys excrete the excess fluid, resulting in clear urine.
snippets.pattern_notes: Causal chain: drink water -> kidneys excrete excess -> clear urine.

snippets.output: Diabetes insipidus is a condition characterized by an imbalance of fluids in the body, leading to excessive urination and thirst. It can cause clear urine.
snippets.pattern_notes: Properties of diabetes insipidus (definition, symptoms, link to clear urine).

snippets.output: Diuretics are medications that increase urine production and can result in clear urine.
snippets.pattern_notes: Properties of diuretics: definition + effect on urine clarity.

snippets.output: Alcohol can act as a diuretic, leading to increased urine production and potentially clear urine.
snippets.pattern_notes: Causal chain: alcohol acts as diuretic -> increased urine -> clear urine.

snippets.output: Certain medical conditions, such as chronic kidney disease, can affect urine concentration and result in clear urine.
snippets.pattern_notes: General category + specific example (CKD) as a cause of clear urine.

snippets.output: If you are concerned about the clarity of your urine, it is advisable to consult a healthcare professional for a thorough evaluation.
